title: Correct t1 value
description: Essential Criteria: Student must state t1 ≈ 67°C (or 340 K) as the temperature where boiling begins at the interface.

title: Correct t2 value
description: Essential Criteria: Student must state t2 ≈ 100°C (or 373 K) as the boiling point of pure B under p0.

title: Boiling point of A
description: Essential Criteria: Student must calculate and state the boiling point of pure A under p0 as approximately 76.8°C (or 350 K).

title: Determines constants α, β
description: Important Criteria: Student must solve for constants α_i and β_i from the given vapor pressure data at two temperatures.

title: Applies pressure sum condition
description: Important Criteria: Student must apply the condition p_A + p_B = p0 at t1 to find the interface boiling temperature.

title: Uses mass ratio in vapor
description: Important Criteria: Student must relate the partial pressure ratio to the mass evaporation rate using the molar mass ratio γ.

title: Considers mass conservation
description: Optional Criteria: Student may calculate the remaining mass of B after A evaporates to justify the temperature plateau t2.

title: Sign error in α/β
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the boiling point formula T_b = -α/β is used with incorrect sign for α or β.

title: Confuses Celsius and Kelvin
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if temperature conversions between T in Kelvin and t in Celsius are incorrect or omitted.

title: Ignores non-volatile liquid C
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student fails to note that liquid C prevents evaporation from B's surface, making the initial evaporation only from the A-B interface.
